quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #7
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: Why is it important to watch for motorcycles?

options.text: They are harder to see than cars.
Motorcycle drivers are less skilled than other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are harder to see than cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and easy to miss. They can hide in your blind spot. It is hard to judge how far away a motorcycle is or how fast it is going. Always be careful and alert around motorcycles.

questions.question: This sign shows one type of:
questions.correctAnswerText: Intersection.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that a crossing road is ahead.

questions.question: When riding in a vehicle, small children:

options.text: Can be safely held by a strong adult.
Are safe if they stand on the floor in the back of the vehicle.
Will not be hurt in an accident because they are small.
Must always be in a proper seat and never standing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must always be in a proper seat and never standing.
questions.explanation: Children need special car seats made for their size. No adult is strong enough to hold a child safely during a crash or sudden stop. Children must always be in a proper seat with safety belts.

questions.question: When a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light, who must yield?
questions.correctAnswerText: The driver.
questions.explanation: Drivers must let pedestrians cross at any intersection without a traffic light, even if there is no crosswalk.

questions.question: When entering a highway from an entrance ramp, you should:

options.text: Go faster than traffic to get ahead.
Go slowly to avoid other vehicles.
Stop first, then slowly enter traffic.
Speed up to match the traffic speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match the traffic speed.
questions.explanation: Entrance ramps have acceleration lanes. Turn on your signal, look for an opening, speed up to match traffic, and merge safely into traffic.

questions.question: Slow down below the speed limit when:

options.text: You are entering a highway with other cars.
You are on a four-lane road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything makes driving conditions worse.
questions.explanation: Slow down when the road is wet or slippery, when you cannot see well, or when anything else makes conditions difficult. You can get a ticket for speeding even if you are at the posted speed limit if conditions are bad.

questions.question: What is a good rule for passing other vehicles?

options.text: Pass on the right whenever possible.
Drive with traffic flow and pass only when needed.
Get to the front of slow traffic so you can see better.
Always flash lights and honk to alert other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with traffic flow and pass only when needed.
questions.explanation: Each pass increases crash risk. If you pass many vehicles, you will need to keep passing. Drive with traffic, follow speed limits, and pass only when needed.

questions.question: If someone is driving aggressively behind you, you should:

options.text: Look at the driver as they pass.
Speed up while they are passing you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move out of their way.
questions.explanation: If someone is driving aggressively, get out of their way. Do not look at them. Do not speed up or block them. This can make them angrier and more dangerous.

questions.question: When parking uphill next to a curb, set the brake and:

options.text: Keep the rear tires against the curb.
Keep the front tires straight ahead.
Turn your wheels away from the curb.
Turn your wheels toward the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking facing uphill near a curb, set your brake and turn your wheels away from the curb. If your car rolls, it will roll into the curb.

questions.question: This sign shows one type of:
questions.correctAnswerText: Intersection.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that a T intersection is ahead.

questions.question: When two vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. You can go when it is safe.

questions.question: What does a diamond-shaped sign warn you about?

options.text: Hazards that exist or may exist ahead.
Food and gas locations coming up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hazards that exist or may exist ahead.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn drivers of hazards on the road. They are usually yellow or orange.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: Circular signs show railroad crossings. This sign tells you a train crossing is near. Watch for trains.

questions.question: What must you do to pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane road?

options.text: Flash your lights at oncoming traffic.
Use the lane for oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the lane for oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: To pass on a two-lane road, you must use the lane for oncoming traffic to complete your pass. Only pass if it is safe and legal.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT happen after drinking alcohol?

options.text: Your reflexes and reaction time slow down.
Your judgment of speed and distance becomes worse.
You calm down and can focus better.

questions.correctAnswerText: You calm down and can focus better.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time, hurts your vision, changes how you judge speed and distance, and makes you more likely to take risks. It does not help you calm down or focus.

questions.question: Why must you be extra careful near a pedestrian with a white cane?
questions.correctAnswerText: They are blind.
questions.explanation: A white cane means the person is blind. Slow down, give them the right-of-way, and be ready to stop to keep them safe.

questions.question: If you feel worried, nervous, angry, or upset, what should you do?

options.text: You will drive the same as normal.
You can drive faster because you are more alert.
Calm down and focus on driving before you start the engine.
Call a friend to talk while you drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Calm down and focus on driving before you start the engine.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions can hurt your driving because your mind is not on the road. Take time to calm down and get focused before you drive.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle with flashing lights is approaching you on a one-way street. What must you do?

options.text: Drive to the nearest roadside and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.
Slow down until it passes you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the nearest roadside and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches on a one-way street, move to the nearest roadside and stop.

questions.question: When should you increase how far back you follow another vehicle?
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Normally, stay three seconds behind another vehicle. Add one more second for each bad condition, such as night driving, wet roads, or high speed.

questions.question: What is used on some highways to show drivers which lanes to use for turning?

options.text: White lines on the side of the road.
White arrows in the middle of the lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: White arrows in the middle of the lanes.
questions.explanation: White arrows in the lanes show which direction you should go in each lane, such as straight or turning.

questions.question: What should you do if your accelerator gets stuck while driving?

options.text: Reach down and try to pull it up.
Shift to neutral and press the brake firmly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to neutral and press the brake firmly.
questions.explanation: If your accelerator gets stuck, keep your eyes on the road. Shift into neutral and press the brake firmly. When safe, pull off the road and turn off the engine.

questions.question: If you reach an intersection where you want to turn but you are not in the correct lane, you should:

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Turn on your signal and turn from your current lane.
Drive to the next intersection and turn there.
Safely change lanes and then reverse to go back to the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the next intersection and turn there.
questions.explanation: Do not make last-minute turns. If you are not in the correct lane to turn, drive to the next intersection and turn from the proper lane.

questions.question: What do downward-facing triangular signs mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to other drivers.
questions.explanation: Downward-facing triangular signs tell drivers to yield. When the road is clear, you may proceed.

questions.question: What helps drivers save gasoline?

options.text: Sitting in driveways with the engine running.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down gradually.
questions.explanation: Quick stops waste fuel because you must accelerate again to reach normal speed. Look ahead and slow down gradually or change lanes to avoid sudden braking. This saves gas.

questions.question: If you are in another driver's blind spot, you should:

options.text: Move forward or backward so the driver can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward or backward so the driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Do not drive in someone else's blind spot. Move forward or backward so the other driver can see you.

questions.question: When you see flashing lights at a railroad crossing, you should:

options.text: Stop and look for a train.
Slow down and look for a train.
Look for a train, then speed up.
Do what the car in front of you does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and look for a train.
questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle at least 15 feet from the railroad tracks when warning lights are flashing. Watch for other signs of an oncoming train, such as lowered gates or train sounds.

questions.question: When can you proceed through a stop sign intersection with no stop line or crosswalk?

options.text: After slowing down to check for cross traffic.
After stopping completely and checking that it is safe.
After stopping at least 20 feet before the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: After stopping completely and checking that it is safe.
questions.explanation: Come to a complete stop before entering the intersection. Then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle, you must:

options.text: Move to the right side of the road and stop.
Wave for the emergency vehicle to pass.
Merge to the right lane and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Let emergency vehicles pass by moving to the right side of the road and stopping. If you are in an intersection, drive through first, then stop on the right side.

questions.question: What does a single broken yellow line down the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is allowed when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Passing is allowed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is allowed when safe.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken line means you may pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: If a police officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light, drivers should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the officer's directions.
questions.explanation: Follow a police officer's directions instead of the traffic light when an officer is directing traffic.

questions.question: If you stop along the road at night, what should you do?

options.text: Turn on your emergency flashers and keep your low beams on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your emergency flashers and keep your low beams on.
questions.explanation: Turn on your emergency flashers and keep your low beam headlights on. Other drivers need to see your vehicle clearly.

questions.question: When may you NOT make a right turn on a solid red light?

options.text: When a pedestrian or vehicle is in the intersection.
When a walk signal is showing for a crossing.
When a sign says no right turn on red.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You can make a right turn on red only if there is no sign prohibiting it. You cannot turn right on red when a walk signal is showing, even if no pedestrians are crossing. You must yield to pedestrians and other traffic before turning.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: U-turns are not allowed.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a red line through it means that action is prohibited. This sign means U-turns are not permitted in this area.

questions.question: When turning left, you must let these people go first:

options.text: Other drivers already in the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic. You must also always yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and other drivers who are already in the intersection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Crossroad ahead. Watch for traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a crossroad is ahead.

questions.question: When must you yield for emergency vehicles?

options.text: When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
questions.explanation: You must yield to any emergency vehicle using its siren or flashing lights.

questions.question: Why is night driving more dangerous?

options.text: There are more cars on the road at night.
Drivers cannot see as well in the dark.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers cannot see as well in the dark.
questions.explanation: It is dark at night, so drivers cannot see as well. Use your headlights from 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise, or anytime you cannot see 500 feet ahead.

questions.question: To reduce glare from oncoming headlights at night, where should you look?

options.text: At the center of the road.
To the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: To the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: If oncoming drivers do not dim their lights, look to the right side of the road. Do not look directly at the bright headlights, as this can blind you for several seconds.

questions.question: What should you do on slippery roads?

options.text: Drive at the speed limit carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down when you see rain, snow, or sleet. These create slippery conditions. You may need to drive slower than the posted speed limit when road conditions are poor.

questions.question: The space you need to cross traffic depends on:

options.text: Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.
Whether there is a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: The space you need to cross traffic depends on the road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.
